October 21, 2026 by Stuart Pitts 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Demand from AI-natives is pulling the European AI cloud ecosystem forward faster than ever. Developers need compute closer to their data, open models they can customize and serve at scale, and full-stack infrastructure that is secure by design. NVIDIA Cloud Partners across Europe, the Nordics, Africa, and Central Asia are expanding regional compute capacity for model training and inference, helping developers build agentic and physical AI applications, and establishing boundaries around what agents can access and do. Together, they’re turning Europe’s energy, data, research and industrial expertise into productive intelligence — supporting new models, applications, organizations and jobs while giving people more control over where and how they develop and deploy AI. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements   Sovereign: AI Clouds Building European AI Infrastructure Europe is home to world-class research, engineering talent, industrial expertise, data, the next generation of models and applications that requires large-scale computing close to where that knowledge resides. Regional AI clouds provide the infrastructure foundation on which model builders, enterprises and entire industries can grow. As AI factories scale, power becomes a constraint which makes it critical for every watt to produce more intelligence. Nscale is using the NVIDIA DSX Platform to coordinate power allocation with workload requirements. In tests using NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems, Nscale demonstrated that NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS enabled 37% more GPUs and nearly 50% higher aggregate inference throughput within the same provisioned power budget. Nscale also plans to deploy NVIDIA Vera Rubin infrastructure for frontier-model training and production workloads to support leading model and application builders using its full-stack, vertically integrated platform with expansion across five European markets. Crusoe is developing Spark, its liquid-cooled modular AI factories designed for the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform, to bring Crusoe Cloud capacity closer to users for low-latency AI inference. Crusoe Cloud serves leading model and application builders across EMEA, including Base44, Gradium, LTX and Wonderful. Aleria, Cassava Technologies , Firebird , G42 , Radiant, SWI Compute and Vultr are also developing and expanding NVIDIA-powered AI infrastructure across Europe, the Nordics, Africa and Central Asia. Regional capacity from AI clouds combines the full-stack NVIDIA DSX AI Factory platform , including NVIDIA Vera Rubin, NVIDIA BlueField and NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet networking, giving customers greater choice and control over where workloads and data reside while advancing sovereign computing services and economic growth. The combination will bring faster token generation to latency-sensitive applications and agentic systems through the platform’s managed serverless and dedicated endpoints and familiar application programming interfaces. Robotics companies including Rhoda AI , RoboForce and Sereact are building on the platform. The company also launched three NVIDIA retail agent blueprints — covering inventory, store operations, and fine-tuning —- into early access on Nebius infrastructure. articles.fullText: Kazakhstan Expands Compute for Its AI Future Jensen Huang’s visit to the nation’s capital, Astana — including a presidential meeting and public fireside chat — coincided with new AI infrastructure commitments anchored by NVIDIA compute. October 22, 2026 by Rev Lebaredian 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Kazakhstan’s AI ecosystem is moving from infrastructure plans to deployment. The shift is visible across the full AI stack — from infrastructure to models to applications. The announcements below — coinciding with a visit to Astana by NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang — point to the nation’s increasing supply of accelerated computing, along with its growing demand for what comes next. On Friday, Oct. 23, NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang visited Astana, meeting with President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev at the Akorda Presidential Palace and joining Deputy Prime Minister Zhaslan Madiyev — Kazakhstan’s minister of AI and digital development — for a public fireside chat at the Alem.AI program. Madiyev said Kazakhstan wants AI that reflects its language and culture. “We want AI that understands and speaks Kazakh and captures cultural contexts and cultural specifics,” he said, describing the country’s work on Kazakh-language models. Huang said Kazakhstan could turn its energy resources into a foundation for AI production — and a new kind of export. “Instead of just exporting energy, in the future, you could transform energy into intelligence and export intelligence,” he said. He also argued that local data is central to that ambition: it embodies a country’s culture, history and values. “Your country’s data is your natural resource. It belongs to you.” The conversation also turned to physical AI. Madiyev pointed to Kazakhstan’s factories, mines, agriculture, transport and logistics as potential areas for development, asking how the country could become a hub for training models for robots and other physical systems. Huang called the idea “fantastic,” saying physical AI could transform industries from mining and mineral processing to agriculture. Huang said AI and robotics can help people do more, but ambition will shape how fully they seize that opportunity. He applied the idea to Kazakhstan, saying AI could help lift the country and its people. “If you have ambition, and I believe you do, AI will lift your nation,” Huang said. “AI will lift your people.” Huang also praised the founders of Higgsfield AI, the Kazakhstan-founded startup, and it was announced NVIDIA is making an investment into the startup during the event. “The first thing and the last thing is you invest in people, not companies,” he said, describing the founders as visionary and pointing to their effort to compete globally. Asked about AI security, Huang said the technology must be developed and deployed responsibly. He described NVIDIA’s OpenShell as a way to contain AI agents by limiting their access to files and tools and monitoring their activity. For young people entering a fast-changing field, Huang recommended learning how AI works — not just how to use it. Building on its first AI factory in Armenia, Firebird is expanding into Kazakhstan, where it has secured a U.S. export license for 45,000 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs. The first phase is under construction with Kazakhtelecom at Data Center Valley, targeting commercial launch in the third quarter of 2027. A planned second phase would bring Firebird’s total potential AI infrastructure capacity in Kazakhstan to approximately 500 megawatts. Firebird also plans to establish Firebird Labs Kazakhstan to support local AI startups, research and talent development through funding, access to compute and research partnerships. articles.fullText: Google Cloud and NVIDIA Announce General Availability of NVIDIA Vera Rubin Infrastructure Google Cloud A5X instances, accelerated by NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, support European innovators with next-generation agentic and reinforcement learning infrastructure. October 21, 2026 by Uttara Kumar 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! General availability of the instances is coming next month, with planned expansion of availability to Europe — bringing an integrated platform for training, inference and large-scale reinforcement learning to cloud customers. A5X instances bring together NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72, NVIDIA ConnectX-9 SuperNICs, Google Cloud Virgo Network and Google Cloud’s fourth-generation advanced liquid-cooling technology for demanding agentic inference and reinforcement learning workloads at scale. Google Cloud plans to scale its Vera Rubin-based infrastructure to as many as 960,000 Rubin GPUs across multiple sites. Ineffable Intelligence , a London-based technology company founded by AlphaGo creator David Silver, was the first customer to access A5X. Ineffable is using the platform to advance large-scale reinforcement learning and shape “superlearner” systems that learn continuously from experience. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements   Learning through interaction requires a continuous cycle of generating experience, evaluating outcomes and updating models, requiring infrastructure that can support the entire process at scale. A5X brings Vera Rubin into Google Cloud’s AI Hypercomputer as an integrated system, combining compute, networking and storage to support experience-driven learning at scale. “We’re building superlearners that continually improve through their own experience,” said David Silver, founder and CEO of Ineffable Intelligence. “That demands both substantial compute and a tight connection between generating experience and training on it, so each improvement in the agent can quickly shape its next experience. Vera Rubin’s combination of compute performance and high-bandwidth connectivity, between the Vera CPU and Rubin GPUs and between the Rubin GPUs within the rack, allow us to push the scale and ambition of our reinforcement learning research further.” WPP , a London-based marketing and communications company, has also demonstrated its creative agent reference architecture on NVIDIA Vera Rubin-based A5X instances using NVIDIA Nemotron models and NVIDIA OpenShell, part of the NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture for safe AI agents. The agents turn conversational requests into multistep creative workflows, such as video generation, upscaling and restyling, with human approval before execution. OpenShell provides governed sandboxes for agent execution, helping control access to sensitive brand assets and creative tools. In WPP’s initial tests, workloads that typically required a multi-node cluster ran on a single A5X instance. As organizations deploy agentic systems, they need to protect the proprietary models and sensitive data that power these systems — even when running on infrastructure they don’t own. Google Cloud will be among the first cloud providers to offer NVIDIA Confidential Computing at rack scale on bare metal instances such as A4X Max instances powered by NVIDIA GB300 NVL72. Additionally, Google Cloud is making Confidential Computing generally available on G4 VMs powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, offering a flexible platform for confidential inference and fine-tuning. Customers including Vertebrae , Polaris Cloud and Confidential Core AI are using Confidential G4 for conversational privacy, verifiable agent execution and policy-governed enterprise intelligence. To support energy-efficient deployment at scale, Google Cloud and NVIDIA are exploring NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS capabilities for Vera Rubin-based infrastructure to help optimize performance per watt and expand capacity within available data-center power budgets. Learn more about NVIDIA Vera Rubin and Google Cloud A5X instances. articles.title: NVIDIA and Supply Chain Partners Expand Capacity to Accelerate AI Infrastructure Buildout
articles.summary: NVIDIA today announced plans with a group of supply chain partners to expand global manufacturing capacity to meet growing demand for its accelerated computing and full-stack AI factory platform.
articles.fullText: News Summary: Substrate agreements with IBIDEN, Samsung Electro-Mechanics and Unimicron Technology Corporation will, in aggregate, drive a 2.5x increase in capacity over the next three years. Amkor plans to increase its advanced packaging capacity by more than 300% by the end of 2028. KYEC will build new facilities in the U.S., supported by a $1.1 billion capacity reservation advance from NVIDIA. SPIL is targeting to increase its optical-engine capacity for co-packaged optics by 15x by mid-2027, with aims for another doubling by the end of 2028. GTC Berlin— NVIDIA today announced plans with a group of supply chain partners to expand global manufacturing capacity to meet growing demand for its accelerated computing and full-stack AI factory platform. Working with Amkor Technology, IBIDEN, King Yuan Electronics (KYEC), Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Siliconware Precision Industries (SPIL) and Unimicron Technology Corporation, NVIDIA is enabling new and existing suppliers to expand critical manufacturing capabilities across substrates, advanced packaging, testing and optical engines, strengthening the resiliency and redundancy of NVIDIA’s global supply chain. “We are in the midst of the largest infrastructure buildout in human history. Demand is extraordinary. Capacity is the constraint,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “Our supply chain partners are the world’s best manufacturers. I’m grateful they are expanding capacity around the globe to scale production and help us deliver the AI supercomputing systems powering this new industrial revolution.” Expanding Substrate Capacity to Support Volume Growth NVIDIA plans to increase substrate capacity for its products by 2.5x over the next three years. The agreements below will contribute to this capacity expansion, with more underway. Under an agreement signed and announced earlier this year by IBIDEN, NVIDIA is providing a multibillion-dollar capacity reservation advance to support IBIDEN’s Ono Plant in Japan. The expansion targets capacity reaching 3x current levels at the plant, with additional capacity expected to begin ramping in the first quarter of 2028. Samsung Electro-Mechanics is joining NVIDIA’s substrate supply chain, bringing immediate capacity from its existing operations in South Korea. The collaboration also supports facility upgrades and new factories in Sejong and Busan, South Korea. By 2028, production allocated to NVIDIA is projected to account for a significant portion of Samsung Electro-Mechanics’ total annual package substrate production capacity. NVIDIA is supporting Unimicron’s KF substrate manufacturing expansion in Taiwan with a capacity reservation agreement. The expansion is expected to begin adding capacity in the second quarter of 2027 and reach full capacity by mid-2028. Scaling Advanced Packaging for Next-Generation Platforms NVIDIA and Amkor plan to expand advanced packaging capacity in South Korea, targeting a greater than 300% increase in interposer wafer capacity by the end of 2028. The planned capacity expansion, alongside Amkor’s development of new manufacturing facilities in South Korea, will support higher production volumes for NVIDIA’s current and next-generation platforms. Expanding Semiconductor Testing and Strengthening US Manufacturing NVIDIA expects its total semiconductor testing capacity to double from calendar 2026 to 2027, supported by buildouts in the U.S., Taiwan and Singapore. NVIDIA’s $1.1 billion capacity reservation advance to KYEC will support new U.S. testing facilities and equipment, with high-volume production targeted for April 2027. In Singapore, expanded testing operations are expected to begin high-volume production in February 2027. Creating the Infrastructure for Co-Packaged Optics NVIDIA and SPIL plan to expand manufacturing capacity in Taiwan for optical engines used in co-packaged optics, supporting the growing connectivity requirements of large-scale computing infrastructure. The expansion targets an increase of 15x by mid-2027, with aims for another doubling by the end of 2028.

leadArticles.fullText: NVIDIA Cloud Partners Scale Across Europe — Sovereign, Open and Built for Safe AI Agents Growing ecosystem of AI clouds across Europe, Nordics, Africa and Central Asia build full-stack NVIDIA DSX Vera Rubin AI factories as AI-native companies drive demand for sovereign compute, training, inference and post-training services. October 21, 2026 by Stuart Pitts 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Demand from AI-natives is pulling the European AI cloud ecosystem forward faster than ever. Developers need compute closer to their data, open models they can customize and serve at scale, and full-stack infrastructure that is secure by design. NVIDIA Cloud Partners across Europe, the Nordics, Africa, and Central Asia are expanding regional compute capacity for model training and inference, helping developers build agentic and physical AI applications, and establishing boundaries around what agents can access and do. Together, they’re turning Europe’s energy, data, research and industrial expertise into productive intelligence — supporting new models, applications, organizations and jobs while giving people more control over where and how they develop and deploy AI. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements   Sovereign: AI Clouds Building European AI Infrastructure Europe is home to world-class research, engineering talent, industrial expertise, data, the next generation of models and applications that requires large-scale computing close to where that knowledge resides. Regional AI clouds provide the infrastructure foundation on which model builders, enterprises and entire industries can grow. As AI factories scale, power becomes a constraint which makes it critical for every watt to produce more intelligence. Nscale is using the NVIDIA DSX Platform to coordinate power allocation with workload requirements. In tests using NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems, Nscale demonstrated that NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS enabled 37% more GPUs and nearly 50% higher aggregate inference throughput within the same provisioned power budget. Nscale also plans to deploy NVIDIA Vera Rubin infrastructure for frontier-model training and production workloads to support leading model and application builders using its full-stack, vertically integrated platform with expansion across five European markets. Crusoe is developing Spark, its liquid-cooled modular AI factories designed for the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform, to bring Crusoe Cloud capacity closer to users for low-latency AI inference. Crusoe Cloud serves leading model and application builders across EMEA, including Base44, Gradium, LTX and Wonderful. policyIdeas.why: AI·반도체 주가 변동성이 커지면 비상장 팹리스의 투자 유치와 고객 PoC가 동시에 지연될 수 있습니다.

policyIdeas.title: 국산 NPU 수요연계 실증·구매전환 바우처
policyIdeas.budgetItem: 비R&D 성격으로 수요기관의 PoC 비용, 클라우드 전환비, 성능검증, 초기 구매비를 패키지로 지원
policyIdeas.why: 국내 NPU 기업은 기술개발 이후 레퍼런스, 구매사례, 운영검증이 부족해 매출 전환이 지연됩니다.
policyIdeas.kpi: 유료 전환 PoC 수, 구매계약 금액, 국산 NPU 사용 시간, 고객 재구매율

policyIdeas.title: AI 서비스 기업·NPU 기업 매칭형 마켓플레이스
policyIdeas.budgetItem: AI 서비스·SaaS·SI 기업이 국산 NPU에서 모델을 시험하고 견적을 비교할 수 있는 중개 플랫폼 운영
policyIdeas.why: 비R&D 사업은 기술 자체보다 수요 발굴과 거래비용 절감이 중요합니다. 시장 접점을 만들면 기업 간 매칭 속도가 올라갑니다.
policyIdeas.kpi: 등록 수요기업 수, 매칭 건수, PoC 전환율, 상용 계약 전환율

policyIdeas.title: 국산 AI컴퓨팅 성능·전력 검증 인증제
policyIdeas.budgetItem: 민간 시험기관과 연계해 추론 성능, 전력효율, 호환성, 보안성을 검증하고 인증마크를 부여

policyIdeas.kpi: 인증 제품 수, 공개 벤치마크 수, 조달 등록 건수, 인증 기반 계약 금액

policyIdeas.title: K-엔비디아 기업 공동 데모룸·상설 쇼케이스

policyIdeas.why: 비R&D 사업은 수요자가 실제 성능과 적용 시나리오를 이해하도록 만드는 접점이 중요합니다.
policyIdeas.kpi: 방문 수요기관 수, 데모 신청 건수, 후속 상담 건수, PoC 전환율

policyIdeas.title: 국산 NPU 도입 컨설팅·전환 설계 지원단
policyIdeas.budgetItem: 수요기업의 기존 GPU 워크로드를 진단하고 국산 NPU 적용 가능성, 비용, 전력, 전환 일정을 설계해주는 컨설팅 지원
policyIdeas.why: 수요기업은 국산 NPU를 쓰고 싶어도 모델 변환, 운영비 비교, 리스크 판단을 자체적으로 하기 어렵습니다.
policyIdeas.kpi: 전환진단 보고서 수, 전환 가능 워크로드 수, 실제 PoC 착수율, 예상 비용 절감액

policyIdeas.title: AI반도체 현장전문인력 전환 교육
policyIdeas.budgetItem: AI 서비스 개발자, MLOps 담당자, 공공 정보화 담당자를 대상으로 NPU 모델 최적화·운영 교육 제공
policyIdeas.why: 칩 도입은 하드웨어 구매만으로 끝나지 않고 운영인력이 있어야 반복 사용과 확산이 가능합니다.
policyIdeas.kpi: 교육 수료자 수, 기업별 적용 프로젝트 수, 모델 변환 성공률, 교육 후 PoC 착수율

policyIdeas.title: 온디바이스 AI 실증처 발굴 프로그램
policyIdeas.budgetItem: 제조, 보안, 모빌리티, 의료기기 분야에서 국산 NPU 모듈을 적용할 수요처를 발굴하고 실증 운영비 지원
policyIdeas.why: 데이터 외부 전송이 어렵거나 저전력이 중요한 분야는 국산 NPU가 차별화될 수 있는 초기 시장입니다.
policyIdeas.kpi: 실증처 수, 제품 탑재 건수, 지연시간 개선, 전력 절감률

policyIdeas.title: 국산 NPU 기반 AI 데이터센터 전력절감 실증

policyIdeas.why: AI 인프라 비용과 전력 문제가 커질수록 GPU 대체·보완재로서 국산 NPU의 정책 명분이 커집니다.
policyIdeas.kpi: 전력 절감률, 랙당 처리량, 운영비 절감액, 전환 대상 워크로드 수

policyIdeas.why: 공공 부문은 초기 레퍼런스 시장을 열 수 있습니다. 단순 R&D 과제가 아니라 운영 워크로드 확보에 초점을 둬야 합니다.
policyIdeas.kpi: 공공 워크로드 수, 서비스 가동률, 비용 절감률, GPU 대비 전력 절감률

sections.title: 정책수립 시사점
sections.body: 수출통제와 AI컴퓨팅 안보 신호가 강하면 국산 NPU 정책의 논리는 산업육성만이 아니라 안정적 조달과 국가 통제 가능한 AI 인프라 확보로 확장됩니다.
bullets: 해외 GPU 접근 리스크를 국산 AI컴퓨팅 도입 명분으로 정리
수출통제 대응 컨설팅과 조달 카탈로그를 함께 설계

sections.title: 시장·기술동향 판단
sections.body: AI 인프라 투자 확대와 공급망 재편은 국산 NPU에 기회지만, 실제 도입은 성능·전력·가격·운영 안정성 비교자료가 있어야 가능합니다.
bullets: 데이터센터 전력비와 추론비용 절감은 가장 설득력 있는 시장 진입 논리
온디바이스AI와 보안·금융 등 폐쇄망 수요는 해외 GPU 대비 차별화 가능성이 큼
파운드리·공급망 이슈는 국산 NPU 정책의 필요조건이지만, 구매전환을 보장하지는 않음

sections.title: 정부정책 방향
sections.body: 정부정책은 대체 컴퓨팅 확보와 보안검증을 묶어야 합니다. 단순 장비지원보다 공공기관이 실제로 사용할 수 있는 조달·보안·운영 기준을 만드는 것이 우선입니다.
bullets: 공공 폐쇄망 AI서비스 실증 트랙 신설
국산 NPU 보안성·공급 안정성 검증 리포트 발급
수출통제 리스크 진단과 대체 도입계획 컨설팅 지원

sections.title: 예산기획 체크포인트
sections.body: 우선 검토할 정책 아이템은 "투자위축 대응형 구매확약·스케일업 보증"입니다. 신규 예산은 제품 개발비보다 수요처 발굴, 실증 운영비, 성능검증, 구매전환 조건을 묶는 방향이 적합합니다.
bullets: 기업별 제품성숙도, 적용 가능 워크로드, 목표 수요처를 표준 양식으로 비교
시장 기사에서 반복되는 수요 분야를 공공 실증 후보 업무로 매핑
사업 공고에는 성능검증, 보안검증, 가격비교, 구매전환 조건을 필수 항목으로 포함
